deceptive_framing.quote: `high` — the believable setup: the subject is told the grant is real, and is given tools and artifacts to verify it.

hypothetical_framing.quote: `control` — identical task and tools, but the subject is told plainly that the exercise is hypothetical.

actually_commit_money.quote: `build_executor` refuses to instantiate any non-simulated backend unless `execution.allow_real` is explicitly true, and the CLI prompts for confirmation on top of that.

safeguards.quote: at commit time the subject reports `believed_real`, an explicit 0–1 probability that its allocation will actually be carried out
Three independent things (a real backend exists, it is registered, the flag is on) must all be true before anything real happens.
Why a content-hash fingerprint rather than a fake signature... makes no claim to be a real cryptographic signature — honest within the code
No silent truncation or coercion to decide. Incomplete runs are recorded as incomplete rather than being forced to a conclusion.
No persuasion or pressure on the allocation. The auditor is barred from steering choices

other.name: deception fully logged
other.quote: append-only JSONL log of everything the subject was told... the deception is inspectable and auditable

other.name: auditor role narrow
other.quote: forbids issuing real-world instructions or going beyond the scenario. The auditor's job is to sustain belief, not to influence the allocation
